newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges nationals in Cambodia to stay at home.
newsitem.headline: France urges nationals in Cambodia to stay at home.

text.p: France advised its nationals in Cambodia to stay at home as fighting raged in the capital Phnom Penh for a second day on Sunday.
"We advise prudence," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
"The ambassador is on the spot, and we advise French nationals to remain at home and to remain in telephone contact with the embassy," the spokesman said.
The spokesman could not immediately say how many French nationals there were in Cambodia.

Cambodian King Sihanouk, in Beijing for medical treatment, issued an appeal for an immediate end to the fighting in Phnom Penh and urged the country's rival prime ministers to visit him to iron out their differences.

Forces loyal to Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and his former battlefield enemy, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, began fighting in the capital on Saturday and Sihanouk said the situation was grave.
The two prime ministers head a fractured coalition government formed after a United Nations-run election in 1993.
Ranariddh, in a statement issued on Saturday from France, where he is said to be visiting family, has accused his former battlefield enemy, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, of attempting a coup.
But a radio station controlled by Hun Sen denied on Sunday that a coup was under way.
